Jim hurriedly crunched the numbers in his head as he speed walked to the door. You couldn't run in this lab unless you wanted to end up stuck with a needle or sprayed with face melting chemicals. Taking off his lab coat and goggles and leaving the lab would take about one minute. Getting down to the ground floor and out to his car would be at least another two minutes even if he sprinted. He frantically started typing his employee code in at the lab exit to punch out for the day before he realized the ridiculousness of logging work hours when every person on the face of the planet was going to die in the next few minutes.

Bursting through the double doors of his office, Jim bolted for his vehicle. He fumbled with his keys, his hands shaking violently from the sudden surge of adrenaline pumping through his veins. The car groaned reluctantly to life as he turned the key in the ignition. Alice had warned him months ago that the car was dying, but Jim had stubbornly refused to trade it in. Jim had always heard in movies that people were 'flooring' the pedal, but he never anticipated that he himself would ever do such a thing. Today, Jim shoved the pedal through the floor.

He turned on the radio immediately after swerving out of the parking lot. When he had dropped off Megan at school this morning, she had dialed the radio into an alternative rock something or other that kids loved these days. But when Jim turned on the radio, instead of crappy pop music he heard a solemn man, reciting a familiar verse.

"Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I shall fear no evil: for though art with me."

Why would that have come on? Jim didn't wait to hear the rest. He switched to news radio, desperately trying to figure out what the traffic was like. He lived close; it was usually a ten minute drive, but Jim was positive he could make it in five if he ran every red light and avoided that fucking four way stop sign.

"Clear roads and sunny skies this afternoon," said the voice from the radio, "If you're looking to skip out of work early on this Thursday afternoon, now's the time! Jim, back to you." What? Jim was so focused on the road that it took him a moment to register that the radio host's name was Jim.

Hurtling along the road, not a power on Earth could have kept Jim from reaching his house. He bobbed and weaved through hordes of angry drivers, each and every one hurling increasingly creative slurs from their open windows. Pulling into his driveway, Jim checked his watch: 2 minutes left. He bounded on to the deck and flung the front door of his home wide open amidst the protesting barks of his chocolate lab, Rocket.

"Alice!" Jim shouted, his voice reverberating through the small suburban home. "Alice! I came home early!"

Dashing through the house, Jim found a note on the fridge. In his head, his wife read the note in a slightly chastising, slightly amused tone, "You forgot about my doctor's appointment today, didn't you? I'll be home around 6pm. Dinner is in the crock-pot. Pulled pork for my little girl and my forgetful man. Love, Alice."

Jim, defeated, slunk into the living room, collapsing on to his favorite recliner. He looked around him at the home he had made with the love of his life. Pictures of Megan were everywhere; in most, she flashed a mischievous, toothy little grin that reminded him so much of Alice. His favorite picture, taken at a random time on a random day of a random year, showed Jim candidly kissing his wife while their daughter grimaced in disgust. Looking at that, he couldn't help but grin. Rocket came to sit at his feet, his tail wagging as Jim patted him on the head. There were worst ways to shuffle off this mortal coil.
